title: RFC: bring-your-own-GPU evaluations for model-optimisation changes
gist: A proposal that vLLM's CI build a signed evaluation image per commit which anyone can run on their own GPUs, with results going to a public database. It states that greedy decoding is not bit-reproducible once batch composition changes, so correctness has to be judged by calibrated task-level tolerances plus a check on token probabilities.
changes: Shows how weak the usual correctness gate is. In the discussion, a standard task benchmark caught one of seven known numerical bugs when they were replayed, and passed a run in which the engine had crashed.
caveats: A proposal, still open; results would be informational, not blocking. The figures come from a comment in the thread, not a study.

numbers.metric: Known numerical bugs caught by a standard task-score gate

bears_on.note: The gate most teams use misses six of seven real numerical bugs.
The open engine is building shared evaluation infrastructure in public.
